title: What's new: Manage PTEs in the Admin Center
summary: This video covers three app management changes in Business Central 2026 release wave 2. The main one is full lifecycle management of per-tenant extensions (PTEs) in the admin center. Upload, install and update are added, with deployment schedules (immediate, next minor update, next major update), cancelable future schedules and an operations page that audits everything. The speakers then cover the deprecation of the old PTE management experience and API, simpler permissions for S2S apps, and early installation of hotfixes for Microsoft apps. The last item is a small change that keeps dev extensions installed on sandbox environments during lifecycle operations.

features.name: PTE lifecycle management in the admin center
features.description: Upload, install and update operations are added to PTE management in the admin center, bringing full lifecycle management for PTEs to one place. Installs are started from the apps page with an install extension button.
caveats: For new PTEs only immediate install or the update window is possible

features.name: Deployment schedules for PTE installs (immediate, next minor, next major)
features.description: When installing a PTE you can choose an immediate schedule, the next minor update or the next major update, plus a sync mode. Previously, installs from within the product could only be immediate.
caveats: For new PTEs only immediate or update window; next minor or major is only for updates to already installed PTEs

features.name: App view filter for per tenant extensions
features.description: The apps page can now be filtered to show different views of installed apps, for example only per tenant extensions. This was not possible before.

features.name: Update a PTE from the admin center
features.description: From the app details page (manage updates) you can install a different version of an installed PTE, which triggers an update rather than a new install.
prerequisites: PTE already installed in the environment

features.name: Multiple future update schedules and cancel scheduled install
features.description: Several future installs can be scheduled for the same PTE at once, for example version 1.1 on the next minor update and 2.0 on the next major update. Scheduled installs show on the app details page and can be canceled before they run.
caveats: Only for updates to PTEs already installed
prerequisites: PTE already installed in the environment

features.name: Operations page audit of PTE actions
features.description: The environment operations page captures every PTE install, update and future scheduling action. Scheduled operations show a target app version and are reconciled to completed when the next minor or major update starts.

features.name: Deprecation of old PTE management (extension management pages and automation API)
features.description: PTE management in the in-environment extension management pages and in the automation API will be deprecated as of version 30.0. Users are told to migrate to the admin center within about half a year and not to mix both experiences in one environment.
features.status_evidence_quote: will be deprecated as of version 30.0 which is scheduled to be released in April 2027.
caveats: Versions scheduled through one experience are only visible in that experience until installed
Avoid using both experiences simultaneously in the same environment

features.name: Admin center API endpoints for PTE operations and easier S2S permissions
features.description: Endpoints for all the demoed PTE operations are available in the admin center API. S2S apps used by partners do not need in-environment registration and permission sets to upload and install PTEs on customer environments.

features.name: Early install of hotfixes for Microsoft apps
features.description: Customers can install a prepared hotfix version of a Microsoft app from the app details page immediately or in the next update window, instead of waiting for safe deployment to reach them. It bypasses safe deployment, so it should only be used when the version is known to fix an issue the customer is affected by.
caveats: May affect users during installation, so coordinate with them or wait for the update window
Environments that do not opt in still get the fix through safe deployment
prerequisites: Know the build number that includes the fix, from known issues in the Power Platform admin center, a support agent or Viva Engage

features.name: Dev extensions remain installed on sandbox environments
features.description: Dev extensions are now treated more like PTEs, so they are not uninstalled during environment updates or other lifecycle operations unless they are incompatible with the change. This should reduce unexpected uninstalls and the need to republish.
caveats: Still uninstalled if incompatible with the environment change, for example an update
